transcript:
[doctor] Good morning, Ms. Smith. How are you feeling today?

[patient] Good morning, doctor. Well, I’ve been better. I’m having a lot of trouble walking lately.

[doctor] I see. Can you tell me more about the difficulty you’re experiencing?

[patient] Sure. It started about six months ago. At first, it was just a bit of numbness in my legs, but now it’s become more severe and I sometimes get sharp pain in my lower back. It’s really impacting my daily activities.

[doctor] That sounds challenging. How often do these symptoms occur?

[patient] It’s every day now, doctor. I can’t walk long distances, and I’m worried about falling.

[doctor] I understand. Let's go through some other aspects of your health. How have you been sleeping?

[patient] Not well, to be honest. I only get about 5 hours of sleep each night.

[doctor] Hmm, poor sleep can definitely affect your health. And how about your movement? Have you noticed any changes in your ability to move your lower back?

[patient] Yes, my lower back feels stiff, and I can’t move it as easily as before. My legs also feel weak.

[doctor] Alright. Have you experienced any changes in sensation or feeling in your legs?

[patient] Yes, there’s definitely decreased sensation. It feels like my legs are numb most of the time.

[doctor] Thank you for sharing that. I see you have a history of diabetes. How are you managing your diet?

[patient] I have diabetes type 2. I try my best, but I’m not very strict with my diet.

[doctor] It’s important to follow a diabetic diet closely. Now, let's check your vital signs and do a physical examination to get a clearer picture.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Your blood pressure is 135/80 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Your BMI is 28 kg/m². Overall, you appear well-nourished and well-developed.

[patient] That sounds okay, right?

[doctor] Yes, those are generally within normal limits. Let’s proceed with your physical exam. I’m going to check your lower extremities for sensation.

[patient] Sure.

[doctor] There is decreased sensation in your lower extremities. I’m also noting decreased range of motion in your lumbar spine and weakness in your lower extremities.

[patient] That’s what I’ve been feeling.

[doctor] Your heart sounds normal, no murmurs, and your lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Everything else appears normal. Based on your symptoms and physical exam, I have a few potential diagnoses in mind. These include spinal stenosis, peripheral neuropathy, and lumbar radiculopathy.

[patient] What does that mean for me?

[doctor] These conditions can all cause the symptoms you’re experiencing. To determine the exact cause, I’m going to refer you to a neurologist, Dr. Amanda Richards, for further evaluation.

[patient] Okay. What will she do?

[doctor] Dr. Richards will perform a detailed neurological evaluation. Additionally, I’m recommending an MRI of your lumbar spine to check for any spinal issues.

[patient] MRI sounds a bit scary. Is it necessary?

[doctor] It’s an important step to rule out spinal causes for your symptoms. It’s a non-invasive procedure.

[patient] Alright, if it will help.

[doctor] It will. I’m also going to recommend physical therapy to help improve your mobility and strength. And we’ll take steps to prevent falls, including a home safety assessment.

[patient] Physical therapy sounds good. I want to be able to move better.

[doctor] Great. Continue taking your current medications: Metformin 500 mg twice daily, Lisinopril 10 mg once daily, and Ibuprofen as needed for pain.

[patient] I’ve been taking those regularly.

[doctor] Excellent. We’ll follow up in 4 weeks to evaluate your progress and discuss your MRI results.

[patient] Okay, I’ll make sure to come back.

[doctor] In the meantime, it’s crucial to adhere to a diabetic diet and maintain regular exercise within your capability. Physical therapy will also help.

[patient] I’ll try my best. What kind of exercises should I do?

[doctor] Stick to gentle, low-impact exercises. Your physical therapist will guide you further. Also, here’s some information on fall prevention strategies.

[patient] Thank you, doctor. This is very helpful.

[doctor] You’re welcome. Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] No, I think you’ve covered everything. I appreciate you taking the time.

[doctor] Anytime, Ms. Smith. We’re here to help. See you in 4 weeks.

[patient] Thank you, doctor. Goodbye.

[doctor] Goodbye. Take care.
